report.answer_text:
The 2025 West Texas measles outbreak was the largest in Texas in years. It had 762 confirmed cases and two deaths.
Cases: The outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, 42 days after rash onset in the last case. By then, 762 confirmed cases, 99 hospitalizations and two deaths had been reported.[1] It began in January, and more than two-thirds of cases were in children.[2]
Deaths: The first death was reported on February 26, an unvaccinated school-aged child with no known underlying conditions. A second unvaccinated school-aged child died on April 6.[3]
Wider impact: The Texas outbreak was linked with outbreaks in New Mexico, Oklahoma and Kansas.[3] It drove the U.S. to its highest annual measles case count since 1992.[4]
